nodes.title: Euler factors of the Hardy–Littlewood singular series

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ be an admissible $m$-tuple of pairwise distinct integers. Then the singular series $\mathfrak{S}(b)$ is nonzero, and the prime-tuple count $P(x; b)$, the number of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le x$ such that $n + b_1, \dots, n + b_m$ are all prime, satisfies
nodes.title: Hardy–Littlewood prime-tuple conjecture

nodes.summary: For an $m$-tuple $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of integers and a natural number $x$, $P(x; b)$ is the number of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le x$ such that each of $n + b_1, \dots, n + b_m$ is a (positive) prime number.
nodes.title: The prime-tuple counting function

nodes.summary: Let $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ be an $m$-tuple of integers, let $p$ be a prime, and let $v_p(b)$ be the number of residue classes modulo $p$ that contain an entry of $b$. Then $v_p(b) \ne p$ if and only if there is a residue class $r$ modulo $p$ with $b_i \not\equiv r \pmod p$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Missing a residue class modulo a prime

nodes.summary: For an $m$-tuple $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of integers and a natural number $p$, $v_p(b)$ is the number of distinct values among the remainders $b_1 \bmod p, \dots, b_m \bmod p$, that is, the number of residue classes modulo $p$ that contain an entry of $b$.
nodes.title: Number of residue classes met by an integer tuple

nodes.summary: For an $m$-tuple $b$ of integers, the singular series $\mathfrak{S}(b)$ is the product over all primes $p$ of the Euler factors
nodes.title: The Hardy–Littlewood singular series

nodes.summary: The empty set of integers is admissible: for every prime $p$, some residue class modulo $p$ contains none of its elements.
nodes.title: The empty set is admissible

nodes.summary: The one-element set $\{0\}$ of integers is admissible: for every prime $p$ it misses the residue class of $1$ modulo $p$.
nodes.title: The set $\{0\}$ is admissible

nodes.summary: A finite set $H$ of integers is admissible if for every prime $p$ there is a residue class $r$ modulo $p$ that contains no element of $H$.
nodes.title: Admissible finite sets of integers

nodes.summary: A tuple of integers is Hardy–Littlewood admissible exactly when its set of entries is admissible.
nodes.title: Hardy–Littlewood admissibility via the set of entries

nodes.summary: An $m$-tuple $b$ of integers is admissible when $v_p(b) \ne p$ for every prime $p$, where $v_p(b)$ is the number of residue classes modulo $p$ that contain an entry of $b$.
nodes.title: Hardy–Littlewood admissible tuples

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
